title: Which way does the wind blow?
hook: Wind generates rotation. Compare measuring rotation with forcing it.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: faster spinning blades go with stronger wind, but the arrow runs the other way.

misconception: Treating windmills cause wind as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: faster spinning blades go with stronger wind, but the arrow runs the other way.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: In a toy world, wind W is equally likely 1, 2, or 3 and rotation R=4W. If you force R=12 rather than select R=12, what mean wind remains?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-windmills-cause-wind/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Wind W=1,2,3 sets turbine rotation R=4W. Filtering R=12 picks W=3. Intervention R=12 cuts W→R and leaves W distribution [1,2,3] unchanged (mean2).

src/demos/probability/p100-windmills-cause-wind/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Wind W=1,2,3 sets turbine rotation R=4W. Filtering R=12 picks W=3. Intervention R=12 cuts W→R and leaves W distribution [1,2,3] unchanged (mean2).

claims.text: Forcing rotation retains mean wind 2; selecting rotation 12 retains mean wind 3. Forcing cuts the incoming wind-to-rotation arrow, while selecting leaves that arrow intact.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-windmills-cause-wind/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Wind W=1,2,3 sets turbine rotation R=4W. Filtering R=12 picks W=3. Intervention R=12 cuts W→R and leaves W distribution [1,2,3] unchanged (mean2).

claims.text: The model makes wind cause rotation. A rotation measurement carries information about wind; changing the rotation variable by intervention does not change the stipulated wind generator.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-windmills-cause-wind/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Wind W=1,2,3 sets turbine rotation R=4W. Filtering R=12 picks W=3. Intervention R=12 cuts W→R and leaves W distribution [1,2,3] unchanged (mean2).

claims.text: If rain causes wet pavement, forcing the pavement wet identifies which rain rate? An intervention on the effect does not by itself alter its upstream cause in the stipulated causal model.
